# Build and validate a clinical ML model in R {.center}

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): apertura. L'arco dell'intera giornata è `fit → tune → validate`,
sul dataset `indo_rct` (post-ERCP pancreatitis). Il deliverable finale è un report
Quarto riproducibile. Mentre carico/scaldo `renv::restore()` in background, anticipo
le quattro tappe: setup pulito, dati ordinati, una spina logistica, lo zoo tunato.
:::

We will spend the afternoon doing one thing well: take a real clinical trial
(`medicaldata::indo_rct`, post-ERCP pancreatitis), and **build, tune, and validate**
a predictive model — ending with a **reproducible report** a colleague can re-run.

- The spine is **tidymodels**: `rsample → recipes → parsnip → workflows → yardstick`.
- One outcome, four algorithms, **one** honest test-set evaluation.
- Everything live-coded, everything reproducible (`renv` + `here` + `set.seed`).

## Supervised vs unsupervised — a one-sentence bridge

Today every model **learns from a labelled outcome** (`1_yes` / `0_no`) — that is
**supervised** learning.

::: {.fragment}
**Unsupervised** learning (finding structure with *no* labels — clustering, PCA)
exists and you met the paradigm in the Overview; it is **deliberately out of scope**
here so we can do one supervised pipeline thoroughly.
:::

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): una sola frase-ponte (cfr. spec §6). L'unsupervised hands-on è
tagliato di proposito (niente carico cognitivo gratuito). Resta concetto, già
incontrato nell'overview ch01. Non apriamo cluster/PCA qui.
:::

## The tidymodels object-map {.smaller}

One spine, reused all afternoon. **Five objects, one chain:**

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {'flowchart': {'nodeSpacing': 24, 'rankSpacing': 32}}}%%
flowchart LR
  RS["rsample<br/>split train / test"] --> RC["recipes<br/>preprocess"]
  RC --> PS["parsnip<br/>model spec"]
  PS --> WF["workflows<br/>recipe + model"]
  WF --> YS["yardstick<br/>score (ROC-AUC)"]
```

- **`rsample`** — `initial_split()` / `vfold_cv()`: who trains, who tests.
- **`recipes`** — dummy-code, drop zero-variance, normalize.
- **`parsnip`** — declare the model once, engine-agnostic.
- **`workflows`** — bundle recipe + spec so nothing leaks.
- **`yardstick`** — `roc_auc()`, `accuracy()`: one consistent scorer.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): questa mappa è la spina dorsale riusata tutto il pomeriggio. Lo
step 04 cambia solo il nodo `parsnip` (engine-swap) e moltiplica per quattro. Tutto
il resto resta identico → "1 cosa, 4 manopole", non 4 pipeline.
:::

# Hyperparameters, one algorithm at a time {.center}

Same map, **one knob at a time.** For each algorithm: *what the knob is* → *what it
controls* → *its effect on bias / variance / overfitting.*

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): le 4 slide-parametro precedono il tuning. Introducono `PARAM/BV`
un algoritmo per volta, così lo step 04 (picco di ampiezza, 10 nodi) non esplode.
Ogni slide è ~4 min. Non si tuna ancora nulla: si capiscono le manopole.
:::

## Penalized logistic — `penalty` / `mixture` {.smaller}

The `glm` baseline, **regularized**: shrink coefficients to trade a little bias for
much less variance.

| knob | what it means | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `penalty` ($\lambda$) | strength of shrinkage toward 0 | $\uparrow$ penalty → more bias, less variance (guards overfit); too high → underfit |
| `mixture` ($\alpha$) | ridge ↔ lasso dial | `0` = **ridge** (shrink all); `1` = **lasso** (some coefs → exactly 0, selects); in between = **elastic-net** |

- Regularization is the **bias–variance knob** made explicit: more penalty = simpler model.
- Engine `glmnet`; both left as `tune()` in the `workflow_set`.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): collega al glm dello step 03 — "stesso modello, con un freno".
`mixture` non tocca bias/variance da solo: sceglie *come* si penalizza (ridge vs
lasso vs elastic-net). Lasso fa anche selezione di variabili (coef esattamente 0).
:::

## k-NN — `neighbors` {.smaller}

Predict from the **`k` closest** patients. The single knob `neighbors` *is* the
bias–variance dial.

| `neighbors` (k) | behaviour | bias / variance |
|---|---|---|
| **small** k (e.g. 1–3) | follows local noise, jagged boundary | **low bias, high variance** (overfits) |
| **large** k | averages over many neighbours, smooth boundary | **high bias, low variance** (can underfit) |

- No "more is always better": k is a tradeoff, not a quality score.
- k controls flexibility only — it is **not** just a speed setting.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): qui atterra la MCQ del min 118 (direzione bias-variance del k).
Distrattori diagnostici: "più k sempre meglio", "k solo velocità", "direzione
invertita". Slide pensata per smontarli prima che emergano.
:::

## SVM (RBF) — `cost` / `rbf_sigma` {.smaller}

Separate the classes with a **margin**; the RBF kernel lets the boundary curve.

| knob | what it means | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `cost` (C) | penalty for margin violations | $\uparrow$ cost → harder margin, fits training tighter → **lower bias, higher variance** (overfit risk) |
| `rbf_sigma` ($\sigma$) | kernel **reach** (how far one point's influence extends) | large $\sigma$ → wider reach, smoother boundary (more bias); small $\sigma$ → local, wiggly (more variance) |

- The two knobs interact: a soft margin (`cost`↓) with a local kernel (`rbf_sigma`↑) are both regularizers.
- Engine `kernlab`; both `tune()`d together.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): `cost` = morbidezza del margine; `rbf_sigma` = portata del kernel.
Si tunano insieme perché interagiscono. Compatta apposta — è una slide da ~4 min.
:::

## Random forest — `mtry` / `min_n` / `trees` {.smaller}

Many decorrelated trees, **averaged**. The knobs control *how decorrelated* and *how
deep* — and one knob is **not** an overfit dial.

| knob | what it means | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `mtry` | predictors offered at each split | small `mtry` → trees more **decorrelated** → lower variance; large → trees agree more |
| `min_n` | minimum samples in a leaf | large `min_n` → shallower leaves, simpler trees (more bias, less variance) |
| `trees` | number of trees | **stability** knob: more trees = less Monte-Carlo noise — **not** an overfitting knob (more trees won't overfit) |

- Engine `ranger`; `mtry` and `min_n` are `tune()`d, `trees` is just set large enough.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): punto chiave da non sbagliare — `trees` NON è una manopola di
overfit. Aumentarli stabilizza la stima, non la fa overfittare. `mtry` è il vero
decorrelatore (l'idea che distingue RF dal bagging). `min_n` = dimensione foglia.
:::

# Step 04 · The zoo, tuned & validated {#sec-04-zoo .center}

<!-- Step 04 (hands-on, 68 min): workflow_set + workflow_map; tune over vfold_cv; rank_results; finalize; last_fit. -->

**Objectives.** Let four models compete — fairly, once.

- Bundle the four specs into **one** `workflow_set`; tune all with `workflow_map("tune_grid")`.
- Tune over **one shared** `vfold_cv(v = 5)`; `rank_results()` / `autoplot()` to compare.
- `finalize` the winner; `last_fit()` **once** on the untouched test set.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): hands-on, il CUORE (~68 min). Picco di ampiezza (10 nodi), ma lo
scaffolding dello step 03 è già automatico → non ri-conta come carico. Un solo
oggetto `folds` riusato per tutti. "Your turn" culminante al min 150 (il summative).
Predict-output al min 165: ordinare 3 AUC prima del reveal (optimism gap).
L'evento è `1_yes` (secondo livello) → `event_level = "second"`.
:::

## Why ROC-AUC, and the optimism gap {.smaller}

**Metric.** With a ~13%-event outcome, "always predict *no*" is ~87% accurate and
**clinically useless**. **ROC-AUC** measures *ranking* of risk across all thresholds —
it does not reward the majority-class shortcut.

**Optimism gap.** The same model, scored three ways, lines up in one direction:

$$
\text{resubstitution AUC} \;\ge\; \text{cross-validated AUC} \;\gtrsim\; \text{test AUC}
$$

- Resubstitution (score on training) flatters; CV is honest-ish; the **one** `last_fit()` on the held-out test is the honest number.
- Here: CV ROC-AUC ≈ **0.628**, held-out test ROC-AUC ≈ **0.538** — the gap *is* the lesson, not a bug.

::: {.fragment .callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Aside.** ROC-AUC is **symmetric** for a binary outcome — which class you call
"positive" doesn't change it (unlike sensitivity or PR-AUC) — so `event_level` here
only affects how the curve is *drawn*, not the number.
:::

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): la winner è la **penalized logistic regression** (glmnet),
CV ROC-AUC ~0.628; sul test ROC-AUC 0.538, accuracy 0.868. Il salto CV→test è il
costo onesto di una coorte piccola e sbilanciata — è IL punto, non un errore.
L'aside sulla simmetria di ROC-AUC: serve a chiarire che `event_level = "second"`
nel codice cambia solo il disegno della curva, non il valore dell'AUC.
:::

# Step 05 · Reproducible report {#sec-05-report .center}

<!-- Step 05 (demo, 13 min): render cached Quarto report + renv::snapshot; pre-hook to Advanced. -->

**Objectives.** Ship the deliverable, reproducibly.

- Render a **cached** Quarto report — it reloads the validated `final_fit`, never re-tunes.
- Close with `renv::snapshot()`: pinned env + `here` + `set.seed` = runnable by a peer.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): demo (~13 min). Il report NON ri-tuna: ricarica `final_fit.rds` e
`wf_rank.rds` dallo step 04 e li presenta — onesto e veloce. MCQ riproducibilità al
min 175: `renv` + `here` + `set.seed` + report cache-ato (non "basta emailare lo
script", non "basta set.seed", non "salvare il numero finale").
:::

## Next: open the model — Advanced {.center}

You built and validated a model. **Advanced opens this very model:**

- **Interpret it** — permutation VIMP and SHAP, with the logistic as a sanity anchor.
- **Go beyond** — deep learning (`torch` / `luz` / `brulee`), and `ellmer` as a typed,
  reproducible LLM-as-ETL.

The validated `final_fit` you just produced is exactly what Advanced **reloads** on
day one.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): pre-hook ad Advanced (cfr. spec §11). L'Advanced apre RICARICANDO
il workflow finalizzato di Basic e fa `predict` su una riga — niente retrain. Poi:
interpretability (VIMP/SHAP, logistic come ancora), DL spectrum, `ellmer`, capstone
`targets`. Il payoff dei pre-hook promessi nell'overview.
:::
